To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of Kosovan students in PISA is determined by parental education and home resources.
the higher the level of parental education and the higher the number of possessions at home, the higher the student performance in PISA 2005.
the performance of Kosova students in PISA is determined by the education levels of their primary caregivers, and the number of home possessions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of parental education and home resources on student performance in mathematics and science in Kosovo.
how the socioeconomic status of students in Kosovo relates to their achievement in mathematics, science, and reading.
the impact of the socioeconomic background of students in Kosovo and how this affects student achievement in mathematics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance in PISA 2005 is determined by the education level of the primary caregiver and home possessions.
socioeconomic factors, in particular parental education and home possession, determined the low performance of students in the case of PISA 2012.
socioeconomic factors are the main determinants for the low achievement of Kosovo students in mathematics, reading, science and overall performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

parental education and household possessions are important determinants of students’ achievement in Kosovo and should be accounted for by any policy that aims to improve the quality of education in Kosovo.
the socioeconomic status of students’ households has an impact on their academic performance.
parental education and family possessions, both measures for socioeconomic status, have a strong influence on student achievement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the socioeconomic background of the primary caregiver and the home possessions of the student have a significant influence on the performance of students.
the socioeconomic status of the student’s family determines the performance of the student.
policymakers should focus more on the socioeconomic factors and not just on education policy to improve education quality.
